output.text: The community garden held its spring workday with volunteers arriving at staggered times to prepare the beds. Assume that Finn is the team captain. Vik won the raffle. Dara and Cleo were on different teams. Cleo and Yara were on different teams. Dara and Yara were on different teams. There were three teams. Finn arrived earliest, well before sunrise, eager to organize the tool shed and lay out the planting schedule for everyone else. Vik showed up shortly after, still smiling about the raffle prize, a set of pruning shears he had wanted for months. Dara came next, carrying trays of seedlings donated by a neighbor, and she was the tallest among the volunteers that morning. Cleo arrived a bit later, slightly shorter than Dara but taller than Yara, and she immediately began sorting compost bins. Yara was the last to arrive, having biked in from across town, and she was the youngest of the group by a few years. Vik, meanwhile, was the oldest, older even than Finn, who was only a year or two ahead of Dara in age. As the morning went on, the volunteers ranked their progress by how many beds each group finished, with friendly competition keeping spirits high. Finn kept a clipboard tally, noting which rows had been weeded and which still needed mulch. By midday, the garden buzzed with laughter, the scent of turned soil, and the occasional cheer whenever someone finished a row ahead of schedule.”
